_comment: xol-inkling - Inkling-2-Mini (26B-A3B looped MoE) on Xolotl's own xolotl-inkling engine.
The GGUF is the official NVFP4 parent (converted with the kept NVFP4 experts); the model is looped, so the
GGUF's general.architecture is inkling2_loop (serve/server.py treats inkling2 and inkling2_loop alike).
The chat template has no generation prompt: the model writes <|message_model|> itself, and the thinking
effort is a template variable (a short prompt system message). Sampling: the model's generation_config.json
(temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, no top-k; 64 is the engine maximum (a request top_k of 0 maps to it).
A small top-k such as 20 makes the thinking loop, a known model-card limitation), do_sample. The 'tokenizer' folder is the pack (vocab.json, merges.txt, token_type.json,
tokenizer.json with pre=inkling2 and special_ids), exported from the checkpoint by tools/inkling/export_tokenizer.py;
without it the server refuses to start and says so.
Pictures: image_pad/vision_start below are the model's own markers (serve/inkling.py writes
<|content_image|><|unused_200054|> for an image part; server.py expands the pad to one token per encoder row,
which the engine's GENI replaces). Two ways to read them, both with the inkling2v mmproj (convert_hf_to_gguf.py
--mmproj; F16 is the ship default, BF16 drifts ~4x more):
in the engine (preferred): add "--mmproj <mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-F16.gguf>" to args, and
"vision": { "in_engine": true, "max_tokens": 1024 } - no second process; ~640 MB of VRAM per picture,
"model": "<the same GGUF as --native, for the vocabulary>", "gpu": false, "max_tokens": 1024 }.
Leave the section out for text only; the encoder is ~0.4B and runs on the CPU in about a second for 640x480.
